mcp_server.title: Shared MCP Server Settings
mcp_server.description: ⚠️ These settings affect ALL profiles. Changes here will impact every MCP Assist conversation agent.

data_description.action_confirm_seconds: After a command, the assistant waits for the device to report that it worked. Fast devices, like most lights, answer right away. Slow ones, like a TV that takes a few seconds to turn on, get up to this many seconds. If time runs out, the assistant says the command was sent instead of saying it failed. 2 to 30, default 10.
data_description.enable_memory_tools: Lets the assistant remember, recall and forget user-approved facts and preferences. Memories persist until you ask to forget them.
data_description.searxng_url: Base URL of your SearXNG instance (for example, http://192.168.11.102:8888). Used when Web Search is set to SearXNG.

memory.title: Memory and personality
memory.description: Shared by every profile. Local embeddings run on this Home Assistant and do not call an external API. Until the model has downloaded, keyword matching is used.

data.memory_include_last_turn: Include the previous user turn in the search

data_description.enable_personality: A short style and persona block that is added to every prompt. Edit it by voice, for example: talk to me like a pirate.
data_description.memory_auto_retrieve: Before each reply, search stored memories and inject the closest facts. Facts stay in memory; speaking style goes in the personality block.
data_description.memory_top_k: Maximum number of remembered facts to add to the prompt.
data_description.memory_similarity_threshold: Minimum cosine similarity. 0.78 suits rubert-tiny-turbo on short phrases. Raise it if unrelated facts appear.
data_description.memory_candidate_threshold: Show existing memories at or above this score and let the assistant choose add, update, or leave them. 0.65 on rubert-tiny-turbo. Nothing is overwritten until the assistant picks update.
data_description.memory_auto_merge_threshold: Only near-identical copies are merged automatically. 0.91 keeps name paraphrases (about 0.92) and leaves different facts alone, including 'Олега зовут хозяином' (about 0.90) and the two bright-white-light values (about 0.82).
data_description.memory_forget_threshold: Semantic match for forget. 0.80 suits rubert-tiny-turbo. Inflected words such as пиратов also match пират by stem even below this score.
data_description.memory_include_last_turn: Also match memories against the previous thing you said, so a follow-up like 'turn that on' can find the right fact.
data_description.embedding_provider: Local runs on this machine. OpenAI-compatible calls /v1/embeddings on a remote server and is optional.
data_description.local_embedding_model: rubert-tiny-turbo is the Russian default: about 118 MB download and 180 MB RAM. multilingual-e5-small is multilingual, about 490 MB download and 700 MB RAM, and is slower on a small CPU.
data_description.embedding_model: Used only for the OpenAI-compatible provider. text-embedding-3-small works on OpenAI. Your gateway must actually serve this model.
data_description.embedding_base_url: Leave empty to use this profile's chat server URL.

error.invalid_json: Invalid JSON format. Please check your MCP servers configuration.
error.invalid_api_key: Invalid API key. Please check and try again.
error.auth_failed: Authentication failed. Please verify your API key.
error.openclaw_not_paired: Device not yet approved on the OpenClaw server. Please approve it and try again.
error.openclaw_connection_failed: Could not connect to the OpenClaw gateway. Check the host, port, and token.
error.invalid_embedding_url: Embedding base URL must start with http:// or https://.
error.embedding_model_required: Enter the remote embedding model name when the OpenAI-compatible provider is selected.
error.access_class_name: Type a name that is not already used. The group needs a name.
error.access_classes_required: Pick at least one group, or choose Not allowed or Allowed to do everything.

access.title: Who may use what
access.description: This starts off, and the assistant works as it does today. Turn it on only if you want to decide who in the home may use which things.

data.access_min_confidence: How sure a voice match must be
data.access_none_reply: What to say when someone is not allowed

data_description.access_control_enabled: What this is for: so each person can have their own yes and no. Required: no. Left off, which is how it starts, the assistant does not check who is speaking and everything works as before.
data_description.access_shared_secret: What this is for: the same password you set in the program that recognizes people by voice. The assistant uses it to trust that the name in a spoken phrase is real. Required: no. If you leave it empty, a spoken voice is not checked and the assistant does not know who is speaking. You do not need a password for messages typed in the app.
data_description.access_addon_url: What this is for: only to copy the list of people that the voice-recognition program already knows, so you can pick them from a list instead of typing. Required: no. If you leave it empty, type the names yourself, spelled the same way as in that program. Who is speaking still comes with each phrase, even when this box is empty. If you do not have that program, leave this empty.
data_description.access_min_confidence: What this is for: ignore a weak “sounds like this person”. Required: no. If you leave it at 0, any match is accepted. If you set it higher, for example 0.6, a weak match counts as someone the assistant does not know.
data_description.access_none_reply: What this is for: the sentence the assistant says to a person who is not allowed to use it. Required: no. If you leave it empty, the assistant stays silent.
data_description.access_manual_people: What this is for: the people you will give rules to. Required: no. If you leave it empty and do not fill in the voice-list address, there are no named people. You can still set a rule for an unknown voice and for people who type in the app. Write one name per line, the same way the person is named in voice recognition. Capital letters do not matter.

access_menu.title: Who may do what
access_menu.description: First make groups of things. Then choose what each person may use. You do not have to do this now: Done takes you back, and you can return later.

menu_options.access_users: People who type in the app

access_class_pick.title: Groups of things
access_class_pick.description: A group is things, rooms, or labels you can later allow a person to use. This step is optional. Without any groups you can still allow a person everything, or nothing.

data_description.access_class_choice: What this is for: change a group you already made, or start a new one. You do have to pick one of these. New group starts an empty group. Back returns without saving.

access_class_edit.title: A group of things
access_class_edit.description: Name the group and tick what belongs in it. A person who is given this group can use everything you tick here. You do not have to tick every box.

data_description.access_class_name: What this is for: so you can recognize the group in the list. Required: yes. If you leave it empty, the group is not saved.
data_description.access_class_entities: What this is for: one light, switch, or sensor. Required: no. If you leave it empty, no single things are added.
data_description.access_class_devices: What this is for: one device and everything on it. Required: no. If you leave it empty, no whole devices are added.
data_description.access_class_areas: What this is for: the person can use what is in these rooms. Required: no. If you leave it empty, no rooms are added.
data_description.access_class_labels: What this is for: things you have already put a label on in Home Assistant. Required: no. If you leave it empty, no labels are added.
data_description.access_class_delete: What this is for: remove the group. Required: no. Leave it off and the group stays. Turn it on and save, and the group is removed.

access_rules.title: People
access_rules.description: Under each name, the first choice is what they may do: Not allowed, Only chosen groups, or Allowed to do everything. The second choice is which groups, and you fill it in only when you picked Only chosen groups. Until you choose, a person may do everything. An unknown voice is a guest, or a voice that was not recognized.

data_description.access_manual_people: What this is for: add people who are not in the list above. Required: no. If you leave it empty, the list stays as it is. After you save, each new name appears above so you can choose what they may do. One name per line. Capital letters are the same person.

access_users.title: People who type in the app
access_users.description: Text typed in the Home Assistant app is not a voice. Here you say which person that user is. Required: no. If you do not choose anyone, the rules for an unknown voice apply to them.

data_description.access_user_lines: What this is for: say which person this is, when the list of app users could not be shown above. Required: no. If you leave it empty, everyone who types in the app counts as an unknown voice. One line: how that person is listed under Settings, People, then =, then their name. For example: abc123 = Olga.
